newsitem.title: UK: Blair says Labour plans do not imply higher UK tax.
newsitem.headline: Blair says Labour plans do not imply higher UK tax.

text.p: The leader of Britain's opposition Labour party Tony Blair said at a London news conference that nothing in the party's programme implied rises in personal taxation.
Blair denounced as "completely and totally false" accusations from the ruling Conservative party that Labour's programme implied billions of pounds of extra spending.
Blair said there were no hidden spending increases in Labour's programme and any changes in the party's proposals would be made clear before the election.

Refering to Labour's plans to focus attention on Britain's National Health Service, Labour's treasury spokeman Gordon Brown said Labour plans to shift resources from administration and bureaucracy to patient care.
Generally, Brown said, the party planned to shift resources within existing budgets.
